text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

--- Denmark's largest department stores, Magasin and Illum have entered the loan market offering customers all purpose loans of up to 30,000 crowns to be spent not only in their own stores, but also in other outlets.

---Danish scientists say 150 million year-old bones from dinosaurs have been uncovered 4.5 kms below the seabed in the Danish part of the North Sea by oil companies conducting test drillings for new offshore oil fields.

--- The Danish government will fight to maintain national rules limiting imports of tax-free alcohol and tobacco until the year 2004 instead of 1999 as ruled by the European Commission when finance minister Marianne Jelved meets EU Single Market Commissioner Mario Monti next week.

--- Opposition Liberal Party leader Uffe Elleman Jensen says he expects a parliamentary election in Denmark next year even though it looks like the Social Democrat-led minority government will now succeed in getting next year's state budget passed by parliament with the help of leftist parties before the Xmas recess.
--- A team of Danish researchers claims to have made greater advances in developing AIDS vaccines against all forms of the HIV virus than scientists in any other country in the world.
